objective: Implement the GameNetworkingSockets adapter behind Transport contract v2 and validate it with the UNCHANGED contract, host/client and soak suites (ChatGPT recommendation after review #4).

expected_result: All applicable tests pass on both transports; skips are explicit; soak gates pass on both.

Defects found and fixed: (1) test crash - null dereference when an expected message never arrived (now a FAIL); (2) GNS adapter did not count accepted reliable data lost on connection failure (GNS stops reporting pending bytes after failure; adapter tracks it itself); (3) client ignored transport Disconnected when already Reconnecting, so it retried on a dead PeerId forever; (4) process-global GNS impairment outlived the instance that set it, blocking the next host in the same process; (5) reconnect reused the old GNS connection, which a restarted host does not know - reconnect now opens a new connection (review #3 answer 2); (6) client connect timer raced GNS's own handshake timeout at 60% loss (3/8 pass) - D-014: the transport owns establishment (8/8); (7) GNS clean leave turned into host timeouts (unreliable Disconnect lost at close; Kill destroyed lingering connections) - Disconnect now sent reliably when supported and close() drains reliable data (bounded 500 ms); (8) impairment mapping: GNS jitter does not reorder (added reorder stage) and the first mapping exceeded the profile's worst-case delay (jitter + reorder each got the full budget; harsh RTT p99 313 > 300 ms) - split the budget. Test changes (documented, not to accommodate): endpoint-reuse test no longer reuses a closed PeerId on connection-oriented backends; exact per-message loss counts asserted only where exact_loss_accounting; raw-UDP and asymmetric-impairment tests SKIPPED on GNS with reasons; new symmetric-outage test on both.
